sections.html: Rachow's Nothobranch (Nothobranchius rachovii) is one of the most popular species of this genus. Most aquarium strains of N. rachovii are descendants of specimens collected in 1958 by E. Roloff near Beira in Mozambique. Other enthusiasts also collected this fish now and then and introduced these strains to the hobby, but they never became as popular as Roloff's "Beira". One of these fish, thought to be a local variety of N. rachovii, was called the "Black Rachovii". In December 2010 the Black Rachovii was described as a separate species under the name N. pienaari.
The Black Rachovii originates from the Kruger National Park in South Africa, where it was initially collected by Pienaard in 1968.
Keeping and breeding of N. pienaari is very similar to that of the well-known N. rachovii. N. pienaari is one of the comparably long-living species of the genus.

Nothobranchius: from ancient Greek "nothos" = false, untrue and "branchion" = gill, referring to the gill anatomy. rachovii: dedication name for the German aquarist Arthur Rachow. pienaari: dedication name for the first collector of the species.
Common name: Black Rachovii. Origin: captive bred.
The fish is extremely colourful and shows gorgeous behaviour while displaying and mating.
